_templatePurpose: Streamlined QuizMaster question set for BCATS Skill Standard 40540 (v1). Designed to keep learner workload low while retaining the student evidence listed in the supplied Being safe assessment resource.
_assessmentIntegrityNotes: Five hazard records are provided as a simple PHS scaffold. The official assessment schedule does not specify a minimum number of hazards; learners still need to cover the relevant tasks, hazards and controls for their own project.
Project-stage photo evidence is repeatable so learners can cover all important stages of their project without a fixed photo count.
Project-stage photo notes combine PPE, other controls and safe work into one short prompt so the photo and explanation remain together on one evidence page.
Workplace before/after tidy-up photos are included in the same Photo Evidence page as project-stage evidence.
Cleaning/check records, damaged-tool reporting and project-instruction evidence remain in the written evidence section.
Teacher observation/sign-off is intentionally omitted in this version, as requested.
The learner self-reflection is supporting learning, not a replacement for the formal practical evidence.

assessments.title: 3. Learner Self-reflection
assessments.subtitle: A short supporting reflection on what you learned about working safely

questionGroups.label: Quick reflection
questionGroups.title: Five short safety reflections
questionGroups.intro: Keep these brief and use examples from your own project.
questionGroups.reminder: This supports your learning; your practical evidence remains the main evidence.

questions.text: Before starting or returning to a task, what did you check to make sure it was safe?
questions.hint: Think about hazards, changes in the area, signs, shared safety information or a quick Take 5 check.

questions.text: How did you decide what safety controls to use?
questions.hint: You can mention removing/reducing the hazard, PPE, guards, extraction, hearing/eye protection or keeping others clear.

questions.text: What did you do before using a tool or machine you were not confident with?
questions.hint: Think about instructions, demonstrations, supervision and checking you understood the safe procedure.

questions.text: How would you safely move a heavy or awkward item?
questions.hint: Think about planning the route, getting help or equipment, and safe body position.

questions.text: How did your safety actions protect other people as well as yourself?
questions.hint: Use one real example from your project.

_finalChecklistBeforePublishing: Keep the questionSet metadata as SS 40540 (v1), 4 credits.
Five hazard records are a local scaffold, not an official minimum.
Project-stage evidence remains repeatable so the learner can cover all important stages.
The Photo Evidence section keeps the photo and its short questions together on one page.
Teacher observation/sign-off remains outside this student-facing version for now.
The live-camera plugin photo-evidence.js v4 can be reused without code changes.
